description: Apply for funding to strengthen conservation and heritage science infrastructure by building sustainable national capability, improving access to nationally significant facilities and addressing unmet user demand. Projects should expand collaboration with industry, to accelerate technology development, commercialisation and knowledge exchange. eligibility: This opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .

To lead a project your organisation must: be a UK registered business of any size collaborate with a Singapore registered business, which must be a separate non-linked entity to the UK project partner or partners

title: Research Infrastructure Renewal
description: Apply for funding to renew, replace and enhance existing research infrastructure and facility capabilities that are demonstrably available to the wider environmental science community. You must be based at an eligible UK research organisation. Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) would not expect to receive more than one application from each facility or infrastructure. NERC will fund 100% of the full economic cost (FEC) of projects. Awards should be in the range of £300,000 to £1,000,000 (see ‘Funding Available’). Projects can last for three to 12 months, and applicants must demonstrate readiness for delivery within the required timescales.
eligibility: You can only apply for this funding opportunity if your organisation is eligible for UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) funding.

description: See the full opportunity details on the Innovation Funding Service . To lead a collaborative project your organisation must be a UK registered business.

title: Resilient economy and security through ecosystem transitions grants
description: Apply for funding for research projects under the NERC-Defra co-funded Resilient Economy and Security through Ecosystem Transitions (RESET) programme Projects will improve understanding on how, when and why ecosystems transition, reorganise or collapse, to sustain functions, strengthen economic prosperity, societal resilience and national security. eligibility: This funding opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility, and organisations who are based overseas. Check if your organisation is eligible .

title: Pre-announcement: Experimental medicine to define mechanisms of gambling disorder

If you are taking the next step towards becoming an independent researcher, you may be eligible to apply as a ‘new investigator’. This is a pre-announcement and the information may change. The funding opportunity will open on 8 October 2026 when more information will be available on this page.

Projects must build on prior Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC) support and include a clear pathway to real-world use through commercialisation, adoption, or progression towards deployment. eligibility: This opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .

You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) funding. It must be your first application to EPSRC as a project lead. eligibility: This opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .

eligibility: This opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .

description: Apply for funding to develop and test dynamic tools and approaches to measure public trust and confidence in policing. The consortium will develop methods to capture the views of the wider community, underrepresented groups, groups who are a priority for policing and their partners, with particular focus on the voices of under-18s and victims and survivors of violence against women and girls. Project leads must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for UKRI funding. The full economic cost (FEC) of your project can be up to £2 million. UKRI will fund 80% of the FEC. The full economic cost (FEC) of your project can be agreed with specific programme areas and STFC will fund 80% of the FEC.
eligibility: You can only apply for this funding opportunity if we have invited you to do so following a successful Statement of Interest .

title: Access EuroHPC supercomputers for AI development (AI Factories)

These access modes support AI and data-intensive work, with a focus on foundation models and generative AI, such as large language models. The calls are aimed at startups, small and medium-sized enterprises, industry and the public sector, as well as researchers. No funding is provided; awards are allocations of compute time. UK applicants are eligible as the UK is a participating state in EuroHPC.
eligibility: Email: DRI@ukri.org

description: Apply for access to EuroHPC’s quantum computers through the quantum access pilot call, run by the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). The pilot lets researchers explore quantum computing and hybrid quantum and high-performance computing, integrated with EuroHPC’s supercomputers. No funding is provided; awards are access to quantum computing resources. UK applicants are eligible as the UK is a participating state in EuroHPC. Check the EuroHPC quantum access page for the current pilot round and its cut-off dates.
eligibility: Email: DRI@ukri.org

title: Access EuroHPC supercomputers for research computing
description: Apply for access to Europe’s most powerful supercomputers through the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). There are four access modes: Benchmark and Development for testing and optimising code, and Regular and Extreme Scale for large research workloads. The calls are continuously open, with monthly cut-off dates. No funding is provided; awards are allocations of compute time. UK-based researchers in academia, the public sector and industry are eligible, because the UK is a participating state in EuroHPC.
eligibility: Email: DRI@ukri.org

To be the lead applicant, you must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for AHRC funding with capacity in languages research.
eligibility: You can only apply for this funding opportunity if we have invited you to do so following a successful outline application.

description: We are seeking director-led applications to investigate mechanistic biomedical drivers of obesity and related diseases such as cardiometabolic disease, and deliver transformative impact in this field. The director, supported by a leadership team, will lead the design and delivery of a collaborative institute. Applications should focus on the key barriers to unlock understanding of the causes and consequences of obesity to enable targeted prevention and treatment. Funding available is up to £72 million for an initial seven years, with the potential to renew. Funding of this funding opportunity is subject to the approval of a full business case.
eligibility: This funding opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .
